responsibility: This file implements the executable target hooks and backend support code for GCC’s eBPF port that cannot be expressed in the declarative machine description alone. It owns BPF-specific function state initialization, target option override setup, registration and validation of the kernel_helper function attribute, emission of target preprocessor macros such as endianness and kernel-version defines, builtin definition and RTL expansion for the special packet-load builtins that lower to ldabs/ldind instructions, soft-fp libfunc registration, operand and address printing for BPF assembly syntax, and target decisions such as disabling unwind info; in short, it is the main C-level bridge between generic GCC target infrastructure and the patterns/prototypes defined by the neighboring BPF backend files.
same_name_distinction: Unlike the sibling same-stem files, this is the imperative backend implementation file: it supplies the target-hook code that works with the interfaces declared or referenced from bpf.h, expands the special packet-load builtins into the ldabs/ldind patterns defined in bpf.md, and interprets option state generated from bpf.opt. It is the executable C layer for BPF-specific behavior rather than the static target-description, machine-description, or option-specification source.
